en: Udāna 3.6 Pilindavacchasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Now at that time, the Venerable Pilindavaccha addressed the bhikkhus with the term “outcaste.

Then a number of bhikkhus approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side. As they were sitting there, those bhikkhus said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, the venerable Pilindavaccha addresses the bhikkhus with the term ‘outcaste.
Then the Blessed One addressed a certain bhikkhu:
“Come, bhikkhu, address the bhikkhu Pilindavaccha in my name, saying:”
“The Teacher, friend Pilindavaccha, is summoning you.
“Very well, Bhante,” that bhikkhu replied to the Blessed One, and he went to the Venerable Pilindavaccha. Having approached him, he said to the Venerable Pilindavaccha:
“The Teacher, friend Pilindavaccha, is summoning you.”
“Yes, friend,” the Venerable Pilindavaccha replied to that bhikkhu.
He then approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. As the Venerable Pilindavaccha was sitting there, the Blessed One said this to him:
“Is it true, Vaccha, that you address the bhikkhus with the term ‘outcaste’?
“It is so, Bhante.
Then the Blessed One, having reflected upon the venerable Pilindavaccha’s past lives, addressed the bhikkhus:
“Do not, monks, find fault with the monk Vaccha.
Monks, Vaccha does not address monks with the term ‘outcaste’ out of malice.
For five hundred successive births, monks, the monk Vaccha has been reborn exclusively in brahmin families.”
“Thus, for a long time he has practiced the habit of calling others ‘outcastes.
It is because of this that Vaccha addresses the monks with the word ‘outcaste.
Then the Blessed One, having understood the significance of this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation (udāna):
“He in whom neither deceit nor pride dwells,
who is free from greed, without the sense of ‘mine,’ and without longing;
whose anger is cast out and whose self is fully extinguished— ”
“Such a one is a brahmin, such a one is a contemplative, such a one is a monk.
The sixth [discourse].
